acceptanceCriteria: A reproduction with >=1,200 dirty .taskman/ projection paths and a CPU-loaded host is recorded with per-phase timings of the dogfood event, identifying whether the dirty-path probe, the index snapshot or process start dominates.

Either the event completes within the adapter deadline in that reproduction, or the decision to keep failing open is recorded with the measured cause and an operator remediation that does not require touching store-owned .taskman/ files.
Focused tests cover the chosen behavior; the fallback notice text still names the measured cause.
body: Observed 2026-10-16 ~19:55Z, corvint from PATH, Claude Code desktop. UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks in /Users/russelllewis/projects/corvint each emitted 'Corvint FALLBACK degraded: corvint-event-rejected:dogfood-event-deadline'. Measured at the time: primary checkout on main ff96980fd, git status --short = 1,266 paths, all under .taskman/ (507 modified tracked projections, 759 untracked projections such as .taskman/tickets/V1-0758.json and .taskman/releases/v1-0-0-rc-2.json); load averages 49.72 51.08 46.99 (a focused go test run, Codex renderer, fseventsd). V1-0881 removed the double probe for ~2,500 dirty paths and V1-1120/V1-1422 covered Stop and adapter kill deadlines, yet every prompt in a long orchestration session still degrades. Expected: the event either completes within the deadline or the dirty-state probe ignores (or cheaply summarizes) store-owned .taskman/ projection churn that the Tasks store itself writes. Actual: no Corvint context on any prompt or Stop while the projection is dirty and load is high. Suspected, not confirmed: the store-written projection in the primary checkout is the dominant dirty-path cost; load alone may also suffice.

title: Hook adapters still degrade with dogfood-event-deadline at ~1,270 dirty .taskman/ projection paths under load ~50 (recurrence after V1-0881/V1-1120/V1-1422)
